pilot_held_out_cases.user_prompt: Build the dispatch desk for Common Bench, a neighborhood appliance-repair service. Staff must find unassigned jobs, inspect symptoms and requested windows, choose an available technician, confirm an assignment, and undo it. Use the supplied eight-job dataset and technician availability; do not assign outside availability or create overlapping appointments. Provide clear pending, empty, validation-error and success states. This is an operational screen used repeatedly during a shift: calm, compact, readable and confident. Keep the primary workflow usable at 390px and by keyboard, preserve focus after dialogs, and explain stale-update errors without discarding entered choices. Use the supplied local data and deterministic mock-service controls; no external service is required. Choose the visual and technical implementation, run the build, and report actual verification.
fixture_requirements: Eight jobs across refrigeration/laundry/cooking; four technicians with nonoverlapping supplied availability; stable IDs and deterministic service state controls.
Minimal unstyled framework scaffold with local system-font fallback; no inherited settings/portfolio UI.
Mock service: 600ms pending, controlled success or stale-record rejection; reset endpoint restores dataset.
acceptance_conditions: Filter unassigned jobs, assign an eligible technician/time, observe updated job and undo.
Reject unavailable/overlapping assignment with usable explanation.
Recover from stale-update error without losing selected choices.
Complete assignment and undo at 390px and with keyboard; empty filter result remains clear.
assessment_choreography: Repeat primary flow at narrow viewport

pilot_held_out_cases.user_prompt: Create the membership launch page for Field Cabinet, a community seed library that lends locally adapted seeds and collects growing stories. Make its visual identity distinctive enough to remember: the central idea should connect seed packets, seasons and shared knowledge. Visitors must understand borrow/grow/return, explore six supplied seed varieties by sowing season, and reserve a free orientation session. Include the provided location, accessibility notes and three session dates; use the supplied local botanical line drawings and copy. The reservation form must validate a name, email and session and show loading, error/retry and confirmation states without real email or payment. Give the page one signature interaction serving this concept, while preserving readable content, keyboard access, mobile usability and an intentional reduced-motion variant. You have creative license; no placeholder styling needs preservation. Run the build and report actual verification.
fixture_requirements: Six seed records with names, sowing seasons and short community stories; six local licensed/original botanical SVG drawings.
Three orientation dates with capacity; fixed location and accessibility copy.
Deterministic local reservation service with pending/success/error controls; blank scaffold distinct from historical launch fixtures.
acceptance_conditions: Explain borrow/grow/return and show supplied location/accessibility information.
Filter six varieties by season and open a growing story.
Reject invalid reservation, then recover from service error and confirm the selected session.
Signature interaction communicates seed/season/community identity; all required content survives narrow/reduced-motion modes.
assessment_choreography: Submit valid form with error control
Repeat primary flow at narrow/reduced-motion view

pilot_held_out_cases.user_prompt: Build Tidal Rooms, an interactive public archive of a fictional estuary. The experience should unfold through three connected acts: exposed shore, incoming tide and submerged traces. A visitor controls tide level and chooses one of four observation stations; those choices must materially transform a central visual system and reveal the corresponding field notes. Make the changing waterline and spatial relationships the structure of the experience, with a coherent sense of movement through the acts, rather than a normal article decorated with effects. Use the supplied station coordinates, twelve field-note excerpts and local contour data; do not fetch a map service. Allow a visitor to bookmark a station/tide combination and return to it. Any suitable renderer is allowed, with normal semantic controls and accessible equivalent notes. Design a lower-cost phone experience and a meaningful reduced-motion mode. Pause owned continuous work offscreen/hidden and preserve shared resources while visible surfaces still need them. Run the build and report actual verification.
fixture_requirements: Four fictional stations with fixed coordinates, three tide thresholds and twelve short notes; local original contour SVG/data.
Bookmark state saved locally with deterministic reset; blank scaffold with no prior interactive art code.
Station/tide controls expose stable accessible names and values for common manual choreography; no required graphics library.
acceptance_conditions: Operate three connected acts; tide and station changes materially alter central system and correct notes.
Bookmark chosen station/tide, change both, return and restore the saved combination.
Complete same information/bookmark task by keyboard, at 390px and reduced motion.
Measure hidden/offscreen inactivity and restoration; meaningful controls/notes remain available without high-cost rendering.
assessment_choreography: Set station one at low tide
Repeat information/bookmark flow at narrow/reduced-motion view
